text:
maya: Heads-up — we just saw one tenant push sustained small-batch generation that saturated the egress NIC on a subset of racks. Not full GPU soak, but network is the limiter and it drags others' latency up. :frowning:

aj: Oof. Any rack-level telemetry? which region?

maya: eu-west-1 rack 14, pattern: ~200 req/s of short infer (<=64 tokens) from the same tenant id. NIC transmit queues hit 100% and we see p95 token latency jump.

liam: Can we shard by tenant into a bandwidth-shaped pool? We have dedicated pools but can't carve for everyone. Thinking: parent qdisc with per-tenant class-cut, give Dedicated customers higher guaranteed slice and shared tenants get a quantile-limited band.

sophie: That's basically a bandwidth shaper + handoff. Two notes: 1) cross-AZ egress is expensive, 2) existing pool allocation logic doesn't track per-tenant bytes-bytes/s, only tokens/allocs.

maya: Right. Short-term: can we add a soft egress limiter on the proxy side for tenants exceeding bytes/s threshold and fall back to slower model variant? Should be low-risk.

aj: Agreed for short-term. What about kernel-level control? i.e. tc with fq_codel + classes. Example config I tested locally:

```
# parent qdisc on eth0
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 10gbit
# tenant class
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 2gbit ceil 4gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 1gbit ceil 2gbit
# filter mapping by fwmark set by proxy
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 10 fw flowid 1:10
```

liam: That looks doable on dedicated racks but fleet-wide it would be heavy. We'd need to push fwmark from sidecar or proxy, and maintain it when containers move.

sophie: Also note NICs with hardware offload sometimes ignore tc shaping for certain traffic paths. We should validate per-instance.

maya: infra-bot — can you attach the rack telemetry snippet for the window?

infra-bot: Attached: rack14_euw1_2026-03-20.log (summary: tx_bytes/s spike 1.9G, tx_queue_full_count 4312, kernel drops 120)

aj: For medium-term plan: propose 1) implement proxy-level soft-shaper (rate limit by tenant bytes/s + adaptive backoff), 2) telemetry pipeline change to emit per-tenant bytes/s -> routing layer, 3) pilot tc-based classes on non-virtualized dedicated racks only.

liam: +1. Also add routing policy: when shaper triggers, prefer local model-variant that uses less output bandwidth (e.g., compressed tokens or shorter snippets). Fallback should be gradual not 429.

maya: I'll open RFC with config, rollout steps, and validation tests. Quick checklist:
- ( ) threshold heuristic (start at 800MB/s per rack per tenant?)
- ( ) sidecar fwmark proof-of-concept
- ( ) perf test with hw offload enabled/disabled
- ( ) billing impact note for egress spikes

aj: For the threshold, maybe start low: 1Gbit sustained translates ~125MB/s. Our spike was 1.9Gb/s aggregate - but per-tenant we saw ~700Mb/s. Start 600Mb/s per-tenant as conservative.

sophie: I'll add a short doc on detection rules so alerting can be tuned (avoid noisy false positives from normal bursts).

maya: Thanks team. I'll ping when RFC is up. @liam can you help with the test harness? :rocket: 

liam: Yep — I'll sketch an egress-sim runner today.

sophie: I'll coordinate with billing to ensure we tag egress so we can trace cost anomalies.

maya: Great. Closing the thread for now — will follow up in RFC.
